title: Changelog generator: ingest model change events, render release note entries, expose internal API for Console/docs
creator: Ethan Park
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelogs
description:
## Summary
Implement the changelog generator responsible for producing customer-visible model release notes and internal change history entries by ingesting structured "model metadata changed" and "model version promoted" events emitted by the control plane. Provide internal APIs for Console and docs-site builds to fetch a consistent release-notes feed with correct public/internal redaction.

This ticket covers:
- Event ingestion (from control plane event stream)
- Rendering/templating into normalized “release note entries”
- Storage + idempotency + backfill hooks
- Internal API for Console backend + docs build pipeline

Out of scope:
- Customer notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond internal plumbing
- Full historical backfill beyond a small “pilot window”

## Why
Today we have model/version changes happening via registry edits, runtime config changes, and promotions during rollouts, but there’s no single canonical changelog for customers. We need:
- Consistent customer-visible release notes (Console + docs)
- A reliable internal change history (Support/CS + audit expectations)
- Strict separation of public vs internal fields (no leaks)

This service is the central "render + publish" layer between model-metadata change events and all read surfaces.

## Inputs / references
- ADR-0143: changelog generation from events vs git tags (decision: events-first, with optional PR label enrichment)
- ADR-0142: source of truth + publishing rules (registry as SoT, control plane emits events, generator derives outputs)
- Schema v1: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/model-metadata-schema-v1.json
- Customer release notes taxonomy/style guide: sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/customer-release-notes-taxonomy-and-style-guide.json
- CI preview requirement: ENG-9826
- Console UI/API integration: ENG-9824

Related PRs (WIP/landed elsewhere):
- redwood/pr-18435 emit model metadata change events from control plane
- redwood/pr-18441 changelog generator implementation + templates

## Requirements
### Functional
1) Ingest events
- Subscribe to control-plane event stream for:
  - ModelMetadataChanged
  - ModelVersionPromoted
  - ModelVersionDeprecated (if available; else treat as metadata-change with deprecation block)
  - ModelVersionRolledBack (optional for MVP, but leave schema hook)
- Enforce idempotency:
  - Event has stable event_id
  - Deduplicate via (event_id) unique constraint
  - Replay-safe: reprocessing yields identical output rows

2) Render release note entries
- Take event payload + referenced model metadata snapshot (preferred: event includes a metadata_hash + full “before/after” diff OR a pointer to registry revision) and render:
  - Customer-visible entry (public)
  - Internal entry (includes internal-only rationale / links / operational details)
- Apply taxonomy categories:
  - security | breaking | perf | quality | bugfix | deprecation | other
- Severity language constraints (per style guide):
  - Do not claim quality improvements without:
    - linked eval_run_id(s) OR “no material quality change observed”
    - and significance qualifier when applicable

3) Store normalized changelog artifacts
- Persist “release note entries” in generator DB (Postgres)
- Provide deterministic identifiers:
  - entry_id = stable hash of (model_id, model_version, event_id, visibility)

4) Expose internal read APIs
- Internal API is consumed by:
  - Console backend (to power model change history view + release notes feed)
  - Docs build step (to generate public release notes pages)

MVP endpoints (internal auth required):
- GET /internal/changelog/entries
  - Query params:
    - model_id (optional)
    - model_version (optional)
    - deployment_mode=hosted|dedicated|private (optional)
    - region (optional)
    - visibility=public|internal (required; public is used by docs)
    - since (timestamp) (optional)
    - limit, cursor (pagination)
- GET /internal/changelog/entries/{entry_id}
- GET /internal/changelog/models/{model_id}/history
  - Includes promotions/rollbacks + deprecations

Response fields (shape described here; actual is protobuf/JSON depending on caller):
- entry_id
- created_at
- model_id
- model_display_name
- version
- variant (if applicable)
- quantization_profile (if applicable)
- deployment_availability (hosted/dedicated/private + regions) (NOTE: public should only show allowed fields)
- category
- severity (info|notice|important|critical)
- title
- summary_markdown
- guidance_links (list)
- compatibility_notes (optional)
- deprecation_timeline (optional)
- source_event_ids (list)
- redaction_applied=true|false

5) Public vs internal redaction
- Implement redaction rules per ENG-9825:
  - Public output must never include:
    - internal_notes
    - incident references
    - customer names
    - raw capacity/cluster identifiers
    - unpublished model aliases / vendor details not already public
  - Internal output may include:
    - links to Linear/GitHub/Datadog/incident docs
    - rollout flags and gating rationale
- Add automated tests that diff-check output for known forbidden tokens/fields.

### Non-functional
- Reliability: if ingestion is down, events must backlog and process later without data loss.
- Performance: P95 for list endpoints < 300ms at 50 QPS (internal).
- Operability:
  - dashboard: ingestion lag, processing errors, redaction violations count
  - dead-letter queue for malformed events
- Audit: generator must log which template version rendered an entry (template_id/template_sha).

## Proposed architecture (MVP)
- Service: changelog-generator (Go)
  - Consumer: reads from event bus (Kafka topic: controlplane.model_changes.v1)
  - Processor: validates event schema, loads metadata snapshots if needed, renders entries
  - Store:
    - events table (raw + processed state)
    - entries table (public/internal rows)
    - template_versions table (tracks sha + rollout)
  - API: internal HTTP JSON, behind service auth (mTLS) + RBAC gate for internal visibility

Notes:
- Rendering templates are versioned and deployed with service (no dynamic template editing in MVP). Template sha is recorded on each generated entry.
- Optional enrichment from GitHub PR labels can be added later (ADR allows hybrid), but events-first for MVP.

## Event contracts (assumptions)
We’re assuming control plane emits events with at least:
- event_id
- occurred_at
- actor (service/user)
- action (metadata_changed|promoted|deprecated|rollback)
- model_id
- version
- deployment_mode(s) + region(s) affected
- public_change_summary (optional but preferred)
- internal_change_summary (optional)
- metadata_before_hash / metadata_after_hash
- metadata_diff (optional)

If event does not include metadata diffs, generator will fetch before/after snapshots from model registry by revision/hash.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] End-to-end: emitting a ModelVersionPromoted event results in:
  - one public entry + one internal entry persisted
  - entries accessible via /internal/changelog/entries?visibility=public
- [ ] Redaction: internal-only fields do not appear in visibility=public output (unit + integration tests)
- [ ] Idempotency: reprocessing same event_id does not create duplicate entries
- [ ] Pagination works (cursor stable) and filtering by model_id/version is correct
- [ ] Docs build can fetch public feed without Console-specific context
- [ ] Metrics exported: processing_lag_seconds, events_processed_total, entries_generated_total, redaction_violations_total

## Implementation plan
1) Stand up service skeleton + DB schema (events/entries/templates)
2) Implement consumer + DLQ handling
3) Implement renderer:
   - map event action/type -> template
   - map schema changes -> category/severity
4) Implement public/internal redaction gates + tests
5) Implement internal API endpoints + auth
6) Wire into staging event stream, validate with 2-3 sample models
7) Hand off to Console team for integration + docs build for consumption

## Open questions
- Do we want entries grouped by "release" (rollout window) vs by event? Proposal: keep entry-per-event, then Console can group by time/rollout.
- Canonical “version” string: use model metadata semver (schema v1) vs registry revision id. Proposal: semver is primary; registry revision is internal-only.
- Private deployment export: needs signed artifact format and offline export (tracked in ENG-9829).
comments: 2025-10-02 — Logan Wright: For idempotency, recommend using event_id as Kafka key and also enforce a unique constraint in DB. Also include schema_version on events so we can safely evolve payloads without breaking generator.

2025-10-03 — Quentin Harris: Please don’t bake model-family specific logic into templates. Keep templates generic and drive most of the text from metadata fields (e.g., compatibility_constraints, deprecation). For “quality” notes, require eval_run_id link or default to neutral language.

2025-10-06 — Connor O'Brien: CI preview job (ENG-9826) will want a deterministic renderer in CI. Suggest extracting renderer into a shared library module used by both service and CI check OR expose a CLI mode in the service repo that runs templates against fixtures.

2025-10-07 — Naomi Feldman: Console needs both a global feed and per-model history with filtering by deployment mode + region. Make sure pagination is cursor-based (created_at + entry_id) and stable under new inserts.

2025-10-09 — Marcus Lin: Security review note—public/internal separation must be enforced server-side (not just caller). For internal visibility, require a specific service-to-service identity and audit all internal feed reads (requestor + query params).

2025-10-11 — Michael Nguyen: Implemented events/entries schema in branch and basic consumer loop. Next: template versioning + redaction tests. Also leaning toward embedding renderer as a package (internal/renderer) so CI can reuse it.

2025-10-14 — Chloe Martin: Console backend prefers generator API to return already-rendered markdown blocks + structured fields (category/severity/links) so UI can be thin. If generator can also include a short 'title' that’s stable, it helps the feed UI.

2025-10-16 — Elliot Price: For docs build, we only want visibility=public and we need deterministic ordering. Also we need a way to fetch “since last build” efficiently; since=timestamp works, but please document clock semantics and recommend using occurred_at vs created_at.
